items.title: Five Conditions for Genuine Correspondence, and Four Origins of Speech

items.zh: 云何相應？當知此相略有五種。一、與他性相應，非自性；二、於他性中，與不相違相應，非相違；三、於不相違中，軟中上品與軟中上品自相應，非餘品；四、於軟中上品中，同時相應，非異時；五、於同時中，同地相應，非異地。云何說？謂四種言說。一、見言說，二、聞言說，三、覺言說，四、知言說。
items.en: What is correspondence? Know that, briefly, this characteristic has five aspects. First, it corresponds with another nature, not with its own nature. Second, among other natures, it corresponds with what does not conflict, not with what conflicts. Third, among what does not conflict, an inferior, middling, or superior grade corresponds with its own matching grade, not with any other grade. Fourth, among grades, it corresponds within the same time, not a different time. Fifth, within the same time, it corresponds within the same realm, not a different realm. What is speaking? Four kinds of verbal expression. First, speech from seeing; second, speech from hearing; third, speech from sensing; fourth, speech from knowing.

items.title: The Four Foods That Sustain Life, Six Kinds of Sequence, and a Third Verse Complete

items.zh: 云何任持？謂四食。一、段食，二、觸食，三、意思食，四、識食。云何次第？謂六種次第。一、流轉次第，二、成所作次第，三、宣說次第，四、生起次第，五、現觀次第，六、等至次第。
items.en: What is sustaining? The four kinds of food. First, edible food; second, contact as food; third, mental volition as food; fourth, consciousness as food. What is sequence? Six kinds of sequence. First, the sequence of flux; second, the sequence of accomplishing a task; third, the sequence of exposition; fourth, the sequence of arising; fifth, the sequence of direct realisation; sixth, the sequence of meditative attainment.

items.title: The Fourth and Final Verse Opens: Eight Accomplishments and Four Objects of Meditation

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：所作、及所緣、亦瑜伽、止、觀、作意、與教授、德、菩提、聖教。云何所作？謂八種所作。一、滅依止，二、轉依止，三、遍知所緣，四、喜樂所緣，五、得果，六、離欲，七、轉根，八、引發神通。云何所緣？謂四種所緣。一、遍滿所緣，二、淨行所緣，三、善巧所緣，四、淨煩惱所緣。
items.en: Furthermore, the summarising verse says: "Accomplishment and its object; likewise yoga, calm, and insight; attention and instruction; virtue, enlightenment, and the sacred teaching." What is accomplishment? Eight kinds. First, extinguishing the [afflicted] basis; second, transforming the basis; third, thoroughly knowing the object; fourth, delighting in the object; fifth, attaining the fruit; sixth, becoming free of desire; seventh, transforming the faculty; eighth, eliciting superknowledge. What is the object [of practice]? Four kinds of object. First, the all-pervading object; second, the object that purifies conduct; third, the skilful object; fourth, the object that purifies affliction.

items.title: Yoga Itself Defined: Four Qualities That Drive Practice, and Nine Stages the Path Passes Through

items.zh: 云何瑜伽？謂或四種、或九種。四種瑜伽者，一、信，二、欲，三、精進，四、方便。九種瑜伽者，一、世間道，二、出世道，三、方便道，四、無間道，五、解脫道，六、勝進道，七、軟品道，八、中品道，九、上品道。
items.en: What is yoga? Either four kinds, or nine kinds. The four kinds of yoga: first, faith; second, aspiration; third, diligence; fourth, skilful means. The nine kinds of yoga: first, the worldly path; second, the supramundane path; third, the preparatory path; fourth, the uninterrupted path; fifth, the path of liberation; sixth, the path of further advancement; seventh, the inferior-grade path; eighth, the middling-grade path; ninth, the superior-grade path.

items.title: Calm Revisited, and Insight's Two Preliminary Schemes

items.zh: 云何止？謂九種住心。云何觀？謂或三事觀，或四行觀，或六事差別所緣觀。三事觀者，一、有相觀，二、尋求觀，三、伺察觀。四行觀者，謂於諸法中，簡擇行觀、極簡擇行觀、遍尋思行觀、遍伺察行觀。
items.en: What is calm? The nine stages of settling the mind. What is insight? Either the threefold contemplation, the fourfold practice of contemplation, or the contemplation differentiated by six matters. The threefold contemplation: first, contemplation through the mere mark; second, contemplation through seeking; third, contemplation through investigation. The fourfold practice of contemplation: within all phenomena, the practice of discernment, the practice of utmost discernment, the practice of pervasive seeking, and the practice of pervasive investigation.

items.title: Six Angles of Insight, Worked Through a Single Example: Contemplating the Body's Impurity

items.zh: 六事差別所緣觀者，一、義所緣觀，二、事所緣觀，三、相所緣觀，四、品所緣觀，五、時所緣觀，六、道理所緣觀。
items.en: The contemplation differentiated by six matters: first, contemplation of the object as meaning; second, contemplation of the object as a concrete matter; third, contemplation of the object as characteristic-mark; fourth, contemplation of the object as moral category; fifth, contemplation of the object across time; sixth, contemplation of the object as principle.

items.title: A Major Section: Attention, Instruction, Virtue, Enlightenment, and the Sacred Teaching Itself — the Fourth Verse Closes, and with It the Entire Second Aspect of Inner Wisdom

items.zh: 云何作意？謂七種作意。了相等、如前說。云何教授？謂五種教授。一、教教授，二、證教授，三、次第教授，四、無倒教授，五、神變教授。云何德？謂無量、解脫等。如句中已說。云何菩提？謂三種菩提。一、聲聞菩提，二、獨覺菩提，三、阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。云何聖教？謂授以歸依，制立學處，施設說聽，建立師徒，施論、戒論、生天之論，訶欲愛味，示欲過失，顯說雜染及清淨法，教導出離及與遠離，稱讚功德，乃至廣說無量無邊清淨品法。
items.en: What is attention? The seven kinds of attention: grasping the character, and the rest, as already explained. What is instruction? Five kinds of instruction: first, instruction through teaching; second, instruction through personal realisation; third, instruction in proper sequence; fourth, instruction free of error; fifth, instruction through miraculous transformation. What is virtue? The immeasurables, the liberations, and so forth, as already explained above. What is enlightenment? Three kinds of enlightenment: the enlightenment of the śrāvaka, the enlightenment of the solitary buddha, and unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment. What is the sacred teaching? Conferring the [three] refuges; establishing the precepts; laying down how [the Dharma] is spoken and heard; establishing teacher and disciple; discourse on giving, on precepts, and on rebirth in heaven; censuring the savour of desire; showing desire's faults; disclosing both the defiled and the pure dharmas; teaching renunciation and seclusion; praising virtue; and, at length, boundlessly expounding the pure dharmas without measure or limit.

items.title: The Third Aspect: Ten Principles That Comprehend the Entire Meaning of the Sacred Teaching

items.zh: 云何攝聖教義相？此中有能修習法。謂於諸善法專志所作、相續所作方便勤修。有所修習法。謂所有諸善法。有有過患法。謂應遍知法。有有染污法。謂應不著、制伏、初應斷法。有障礙法。謂違逆現觀究竟法。有隨順法。謂隨順現觀究竟法。有真如所攝法。謂應覺悟法。有勝德所攝法。謂所應引發法。有隨順世間法。謂應習、應斷，及斷已現行法。有得究竟法。謂究竟自義所應證法。
items.en: What is the aspect comprehending the meaning of the sacred teaching? Herein there is the phenomenon of being able to cultivate — namely, the diligent cultivation of wholesome phenomena through devoted application and unbroken application. There is the phenomenon to be cultivated — namely, all wholesome phenomena. There is the phenomenon possessing faults — namely, that which is to be thoroughly known. There is the phenomenon possessing defilement — namely, that which is not to be clung to, is to be subdued, and is, at the outset, to be severed. There is the obstructing phenomenon — namely, that which runs contrary to the consummation of direct realisation. There is the conforming phenomenon — namely, that which conforms to the consummation of direct realisation. There is the phenomenon comprised by suchness — namely, that which is to be awakened to. There is the phenomenon comprised by excellent virtue — namely, that which is to be elicited. There is the phenomenon conforming to the world — namely, that which is to be cultivated, that which is to be severed, and that which continues to manifest once already severed. There is the phenomenon of attaining the ultimate — namely, that which is to be realised as one's own ultimate aim.

items.title: The Fourth and Final Aspect Opens: Three Ways Beings Continue Living, and the Roots of Delusion, Defilement, and Suffering

items.zh: 當知此中，一切有情住有三種。謂日別住、盡壽住、善法可愛生展轉住。初由食增上力，第二由命行增上力，第三由於諸善法不放逸增上力。於諸不善、無記法中、亦有相似不放逸法，如於殺生等事及威儀工巧等中審諦而作。然於善法不放逸者，於現法中乃至能得般涅槃故、於後法中往善趣故，多有所作。復次，依有情世間及器世間，有二種法，能攝一切諸戲論事。謂能取法，及彼所依、所取之法。又諸世間略有二種雜染根本，能引無義無利雜染。謂於真實無正解行，及彼為先悕求無義。又正法外，若諸沙門、若婆羅門，略有二種雜染根本。謂薩迦耶見增上力故，推求我常，推求我斷。又諸有情略有二種眾苦根本。謂於有漏法喜愛俱行所有期願，及非理所引厭離俱行所有期願。
items.en: Know that herein, all sentient beings continue in three ways: continuing day by day, continuing for the span of a lifetime, and continuing on through the mutual perpetuation of wholesome conduct and agreeable rebirth. The first is by the power of food; the second, by the power of the life-force; the third, by the power of diligence in wholesome phenomena. Furthermore, in dependence on the world of sentient beings and the world of their environment, there are two phenomena that comprehend the entirety of discursive proliferation: the grasping phenomena, and the phenomena they depend on and grasp at. Furthermore, in the world at large there are, briefly, two root defilements that give rise to meaningless, unbeneficial defilement: the absence of correct understanding regarding what is real, and the meaningless craving that this absence gives rise to. Furthermore, sentient beings have, briefly, two root sufferings: the yearning that accompanies delight in phenomena subject to outflow, and the yearning that accompanies an unreasoned aversion [to existence itself].

blocks.text: Today's reading reaches the fourth and last verse of key terms, which concerns practice itself: what "yoga" means, and how calm and insight are cultivated. The Stage Attained Through Hearing thus ends its list of what must be learned with the practice that learning is for.
Five conditions make for genuine correspondence between mind and its factors (Day 3); speech has four origins.

The four foods again (Days 13, 32). Venerable Miào Jìng on **mental volition as food**: "When there's hope, though the thing isn't done yet, the mind is happy, and this nourishes the faculties and elements." Hope sustains life; despair erodes it.

Practice accomplishes eight things: extinguishing the basis, transforming the basis, knowing the object, delighting in the object, attaining the fruit, and more. Venerable Miào Jìng: "thoroughly knowing the object" concerns the truths of suffering and origin; "delighting in the object" concerns cessation and the path. Four objects of meditation are named: the pervasive object, the object that purifies conduct, the skilful object, and the object that purifies afflictions, which the *Śrāvakabhūmi* develops at length.

"**Yoga**" has four kinds: **faith**, **aspiration**, **diligence**, and **skilful means**. This is the treatise's own definition of the word in its title (Introduction 2). Yoga is not a posture or a technique; it is faith that the path is real, aspiration to walk it, diligence in walking, and skill in method. Nine stages of the path follow.

**Calm** (止) is revisited, and **insight** (觀) is explained through preliminary schemes. The threefold contemplation: seeking, investigation, and examination. Venerable Miào Jìng distinguishes them in skeleton contemplation: seeking is rough, imagining the skeleton from head to foot and back; investigation is finer, examining each part.

Six angles of insight are then worked through a single example, contemplating the body's impurity: its meaning, its thing, its mark, its category, its time, and its reasoning. This six-angle method recurs in the *Śrāvakabhūmi* as the standard way to investigate any object.

The third aspect of inner wisdom: ten principles that comprehend the whole meaning of the noble teaching. The fourth aspect opens with three ways beings continue living, and the roots of delusion, defilement, and suffering. Tomorrow's reading completes it.

quiz.q: In mutual relation, "if one phenomenon can draw forth another, they are related." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain this?
options: the six faculties and six consciousnesses — the bases draw forth consciousness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "It should be the six faculties and six consciousnesses — the six bases draw forth the six consciousnesses." Master Cháng Bǎi agrees; dependent origination is the *Pixunji*'s alternative. The reading note gives only the latter.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "mental volition as food"?
options: when there's hope, even before something is done, the mind is happy — and that nourishes the faculties and elements
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When there's hope, though the thing isn't done yet, the mind is happy — and this nourishes the faculties and elements." The text: sustaining is the four foods. Master Cháng Bǎi: arhats cut craving for all four.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the eight accomplishments?
options: extinguishing the basis, transforming the basis, knowing the object, delighting in the object, attaining the fruit, freedom from desire, transforming the faculty, eliciting superknowledge
quiz.why: "First, extinguishing the basis; second, transforming the basis; third, thoroughly knowing the object; fourth, delighting in the object; fifth, attaining the fruit; sixth, becoming free of desire; seventh, transforming the faculty; eighth, eliciting superknowledge." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first four are the work; the last four its fruits.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng correlate "thoroughly knowing the object" and "delighting in the object"?
options: knowing concerns the truths of suffering and origin; delighting concerns cessation and the path
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Thoroughly knowing the object concerns the truths of suffering and origin"; "delighting in the object concerns cessation and the path — the path being discipline, concentration, and wisdom." The reading note's generic reading differs.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the four kinds of yoga?
quiz.why: "The four kinds of yoga: first, faith; second, aspiration; third, diligence; fourth, skilful means." The nine kinds are the worldly, supramundane, preparatory, uninterrupted, liberation, and advancement paths, and three grades. Venerable Miào Jìng: faith and aspiration rise in proportion.

quiz.q: In the threefold contemplation, how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish seeking and investigation?
options: exploring the unknown vs. reviewing the known
seeking is rough reflection — imagining the skeleton head to foot and back; investigation is finer
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Seeking is rough reflection — in skeleton contemplation, merely imagining from head to foot and foot to head." Calm and insight strengthen each other. The reading note's division differs.
